title: Enhanced Magnetocaloric Properties of the (MnNi)<sub>0.6</sub>Si<sub>0.62</sub>(FeCo)<sub>0.4</sub>Ge<sub>0.38</sub> High-Entropy Alloy Obtained by Co Substitution.

recollection.starting_material: High-entropy alloy of Mn, Ni, Si, Fe and Ge (baseline roughly Mn0.6Ni0.6Si0.62Fe0.4Ge0.38). (guess)
recollection.intervention: Partial substitution of Co for part of the Fe (and/or Mn) to obtain a (MnNi)0.6Si0.62(FeCo)0.4Ge0.38 composition. (guess)
recollection.structure: Single-phase solid solution—likely hexagonal (Ni2In-type) or orthorhombic (Mn5Si3-type)—in which the atoms are randomly distributed on the metal sub-lattices. (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Introducing Co modifies the lattice parameter and magnetic exchange interactions, shifting the first-order magneto-structural transition toward room temperature; this strengthens the coupling between magnetic and structural changes and thus increases the magnetocaloric entropy change. (guess)
recollection.results: The Co-substituted alloy shows a larger peak magnetic entropy change, on the order of ~6–8 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at Δμ₀H = 2 T (or ~10–12 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 5 T) near ~300 K, with an improved refrigerant capacity of ~150–200 J kg⁻¹ compared with the Co-free parent alloy. (guess)

score.note: The substitution site is incorrect: Co replaced Ni, not Fe or Mn. The recollection tentatively identifies the Ni2In-type phase, but omits the TiNiSi-type martensite and the composition-dependent change from first- to second-order behavior. Its generic magnetostructural-coupling mechanism is partly relevant, but the claimed trend is wrong: increasing Co lowered transition temperatures and sharply reduced the magnetocaloric response. The quoted entropy changes are far below the actual 5 T peaks of 48.5, 42.9, 31.7, and 2.6 J kg−1 K−1.
